sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.text_preview: C LOCKING at gigahertz rates requires generators with low skew and low jitter to avoid synchronous timing failures. The notion of a “clocking surface” becomes untenable at gigahertz rates [1], frequently mandating that large VLSI chips are subdivided into multiple clock domains and/or utilize skew-tolerant multiphase circuit design techniques [2]. sections.title: CONCLUSION AND FURTHER WORK PLANNED
sections.text_preview: This paper has described the rotary traveling-wave oscillator (RTWO) and its potential application to gigahertz-rate VLSI clocking. The oscillator is unique for a resonant-style LC-based oscillator in that it produces square waves directly and can be hardwired to form rotary oscillator arrays (ROAs).
